bottleneck: CAR-T therapy can trigger cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity severe enough to require ICU care, driven by massive immune activation when engineered cells engage their targets. On-target, off-tumor effects — killing healthy cells that share the antigen — add another lethal risk, as seen with targets expressed at low levels on normal tissue. Toxicity management, not efficacy, often defines the therapeutic window.
current_state: Tocilizumab and steroids manage CRS, and suicide switches allow emergency shutoff, but these are rescues, not prevention. Safer antigen targets and tunable CARs are active research.

sources.title: Gene Therapy: A Breakthrough in Disease Treatment

title: CAR-T cytokine storms and off-tumor toxicity
why_it_blocks: A therapy that can kill the patient as easily as the cancer cannot move to earlier lines of treatment or outpatient use. Taming toxicity is the precondition for cell therapy's expansion.
